title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 85-86
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 85 to 86 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 85 to 86 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 85 to 86.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 85 to 86** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः । अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी ॥** **सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः । महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः ॥**

The source of the world, beautiful and full of joy is he. A jewel-like navel and lovely eyes belong to that God of gods. The Sun, the giver of food, the horned one, Jayanta, the knower of all who is ever victorious. Golden-flecked, never shaken, the Lord even of the lords of speech is he. The great lake, the great abyss, the great being and the great treasure is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 85 to 86 mean?
faq.a: The source of the world, beautiful and full of joy is he. A jewel-like navel and lovely eyes belong to that God of gods. The Sun, the giver of food, the horned one, Jayanta, the knower of all who is ever victorious. Golden-flecked, never shaken, the Lord even of the lords of speech is he. The great lake, the great abyss, the great being and the great treasure is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
